name: ShapeNet-SRN
ability_definition: The ability to imagine how something will look after it is moved around or when its parts are moved or rearranged.

task_realism.reasoning: Predicting how an object looks from a rotated viewpoint directly mirrors the 'after it is moved around' part of the ability. Workers such as drafters, mechanics, and designers do this when they picture a part from another angle. However, the tasks are synthetic untextured-to-lightly-textured renders of chairs and cars from a single category. The model is trained on thousands of same-category examples, so it can lean on learned category priors rather than generalized mental transformation.

evaluation_conditions.reasoning: Inputs are clean 128x128 renders with no background, controlled lighting, and fixed camera distance on a viewing sphere. Train and test sets come from the same narrow category. Real work involves cluttered scenes, novel object types, partial occlusion, and functional stakes such as fit and clearance. There is no time pressure or out-of-distribution generalization comparable to real use.

construct_coverage.reasoning: It covers only whole-object rigid viewpoint change. It omits rearranging or moving parts, assembly and disassembly, folding, and articulated motion. The PSNR metric conflates spatial correctness with pixel fidelity and rewards blurry averaged predictions. Category-specific training further narrows what is actually measured.

format_match.reasoning: Image-in, image-out is more natural than multiple choice. Producing a rendered view loosely resembles sketching or CAD previews. But real work artifacts are usually decisions, annotated drawings, or 3D models of arbitrary objects, not low-resolution synthetic renders scored by pixel error.

transferability_reasoning: ShapeNet-SRN tests a genuine slice of visualization, predicting an object's appearance after rotation, in a generative format. That slice is confined to synthetic, single-category, clean renders and is scored by a fidelity metric that mixes image quality with spatial understanding. It omits part rearrangement entirely and permits reliance on category priors, so it is only a weak proxy for workplace visualization ability.

2020.human_reference: General adult workforce performing everyday spatial visualization (imagining how a familiar object such as a chair or car looks from another viewpoint), benchmarked against typical mental-rotation competence.
